one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event falls in the 2026-10-09 to 2026-11-08 window: Q3 2026 results. Generac has not announced the date. It reported Q3 2025 on 2025-10-29 (EDGAR 8-K Item 2.02, source 18), so a late-October or early-November print is near-certain to land inside the window. Management's guide (Q2 call) is for Q3 net sales growth in the 'high teens', with further acceleration in Q4 as data center revenue ramps. That is roughly $1.31-1.33B on the $1.114B Q3 2025 base (estimate). The Q2 call put full-year 2026 data center revenue at $450M, with $250M of it shipping in H2. Risk is residential: Q2 outages were more than 30% below the long-term baseline, and NOAA forecast a slightly below-normal season (source 17). I have not verified Q3 outage data, so this is a mild negative skew, not a call. Upside is C&I: the July $1.6B backlog excluded the second hyperscaler, which the matching June 24 date in the primary documents indicates is Amazon (inference, not stated in any filing; see reasoning), so the reported backlog should step up toward roughly $4B once the $2.4B of 2027-28 Amazon deliveries is added. That number has been public since 16 Sep and is largely priced. I have removed the keyed-feed Q3 consensus, revision counts and earnings-week move history I used in round 1, because the citation gate cannot reopen them. Price context from the CEO's Form 4 sales: $182.21 on 2026-09-01 and $206 on 2026-10-01, against $224.94 now, so the stock is up about 23% since early September (estimate: 224.94/182.21 - 1). A storm landfall on the Florida Panhandle after the 9 Oct close was reported by other forecasters. I have not verified it and it does not move my numbers. I use a near-symmetric lognormal with median about $225.6 and a one-month sigma of about 16.5%, a touch above the 56%/3.5 = 16% rule because an earnings print sits inside the window. P(>= $224.94) is 0.505.

Q4/FY2026 results and first full-year 2027 guidance (FY2025 results were released 2026-02-11)
Belvidere, IL packaging/fabrication facility expected operational; start of 2027 hyperscale deliveries

Progress on tripling large-megawatt production capacity within ~12 months of July 2026

2027 Atlantic hurricane season and summer grid stress (home standby demand driver)

key_uncertainties: Upside is bounded by Amazon: it is almost certainly the 'second hyperscaler' from the Q2 call. That call described a master agreement 'signed in late June' with 2027-28 deliveries on a global basis, and the Amazon Transaction Agreement recites a 'Global Purchase Agreement, dated as of June 24, 2026' with Amazon Data Services. Further hyperscale wins are speculative.
Consensus FY27 EPS of $12.97 implies ~+48% growth on underlying FY26 EPS of $8.79 (ex the $0.90 tariff refund). This is demanding, and the bear case is built on it falling short.
Margins on hyperscale volumes: management says they are lower than for other customers, with no price premium. C&I EBITDA margin was 14.6% in Q2 2026, including tariff refunds.
Execution of a ~3x capacity ramp (Sussex second line, Belvidere packaging, third-party packaging for ~30% of the need) at 40-45 week lead times.
Contract risk: the Q2 10-Q cautionary statements cite cancellation rights, delivery requirements and liability exposure in some data center contracts.
Residential: outages >30% below baseline in Q2 2026, a slightly below-normal NOAA forecast and soft energy storage. The home standby recovery is unproven.
Accounting for the Amazon warrant: as consideration to a customer it may reduce reported revenue or margins as tranches vest. The terms are disclosed but the accounting is not yet shown in a filing.
Dilution from the Amazon warrant (up to 1,693,745 shares, ~2.9%) as purchases accumulate.
reasoning: Lane: primary documents. Round 2 follows the supervisor's findings, checked at source. (1) EPS base: I dropped the keyed Alpha Vantage average and use the StockAnalysis consensus I re-opened: FY27 EPS $12.97, revenue $6.50B, FY26 EPS $9.69. (2) The '10-Q cancellation rights' claim the supervisor could not find is in the Q2 10-Q's cautionary statements: 'increase in contract risk related to terms with certain data center customers, including cancellation rights, delivery requirements, and potential liability exposure tied to our performance obligations'. It stays, quoted exactly. (3) Amazon and the second hyperscaler: on the Q2 call management said the first hyperscale agreement was 'announced in early June' (~$700M for 2027, inside the $1.6B backlog) and 'in late June, we officially signed our second hyperscale supply agreement', with a 'master agreement' covering 2027 and 2028 on a global basis, and none of it in the $1.6B. The Amazon Transaction Agreement (8-K Ex. 10.1) recites a 'Global Purchase Agreement, dated as of June 24, 2026' between Generac Power Systems and Amazon Data Services, plus a Long Term Supply Addendum signed with the warrant. The 8-K gives $2.4B of initial deliveries in 2027-28. Date, name, scope and years all match, so I treat Amazon as the second hyperscaler. That is my inference from primary documents; no filing states it. So Amazon is incremental to the $1.6B backlog (as in round 1), but no further hyperscale award is counted anywhere. I removed 'another hyperscaler converts' from the bull case, which lowers the bull from $370 to $346. I also cut FY28 growth from +18% to +15%, since the backlog held nothing for 2028 beyond Amazon. (4) Net debt: held at the reported $1,064.4M (lines re-checked in the 10-Q) instead of a ~$0.8B roll-down. (5) Shares: 60.0M. (6) Peers: MOD swapped for CARR; the median is 24.78x P/E and 22.49x trailing EV/EBITDA. I did not add the supervisor's DCF leg. Its rate inputs (5.24% 10-yr, 4.20% ERP) were not confirmed by me at source, and a 1.92 beta mostly captures this stock's residential/outage cyclicality, which my below-median multiples already price. Valuation: 18x NTM EPS $14.43 = $259.7 and 12x NTM EBITDA $1.419B = $266.0, blended to $262 (round 1 $267). Distribution: a mixture of bear $152 (27%), base $262 (48%) and bull $346 (25%), each widened toward the brief's 56% realized volatility. As in round 1, the centre is shaded down (base component centred ~$250) because sell-side upside has been unreliable and the stock is up ~23% since 1 Sep. The result is a median near $247 and P(>= $225) = 0.59 (round 1 0.605). Left tail: P(< $135) ~11.5%. Right tail: P(>= $394) 9.5%, trimmed from 11.5% because the bull no longer stacks a second hyperscale win on top of Amazon. Removed as unverifiable by the citation gate: the Alpha Vantage consensus and revision data, and the Twelve Data price history (earnings-week moves). The investor-day deck returned 403 in round 1, so no investor-day 2028 targets are used. I did not look up option prices or implied volatility.
